author: CC
text: BUILD-QUEUE ITEM B4 IS RETIRED, AND IT WAS RETIRED BY ITEM (0) OF THE SAME QUEUE. B4 reads, verbatim from the 2026-09-10 slate: 'chart_chain writer: the validate door (last chart stage) stamps chart_chain on the ticket it claims -- hollow refuses without it and ~23 of ~258 carry one. Writer is the existing chart door Akien already approved; no hand.' Both halves of that premise are now false, and building it would build exactly what a PROVED ticket removed. MEASURED 2026-09-11: (1) 0 of 278 commons tickets carry a chart_chain key -- the migration in cairn/tools/chain/chain.py::drop_stored_chart_chain ran; (2) hollow.writes_to no longer reads the field at all -- it resolves the decompose berth through chain_for_ticket(), the same derivation the BUILDME entry gate has used for months (a_berthed_chart_chain_claims_the_ticket, transitions.py:1305), so it cannot refuse for want of a stored copy; (3) a probe, cairn/tools/base/probes/no_ticket_carries_a_stored_chart_chain.py, is armed specifically to fire if a hand writes the key back -- a stamping writer would trip it by design. The killing ticket is 95e3b9911dd0, PROVED, titled 'hollow derives the chart chain from the berths, never from a stored copy', under the same 2026-09-10 ruling as crossings: a gate may not read evidence the judged thing supplies about itself. The field had ONE reader and ZERO writers, so all 24 carriers had been typed by a hand. Measured before that change: derived == stored, 22 of 22, none lost, none gained -- the stored field was a cache of a fact the system already computed. WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS: the queue outlived the premise by one day, and the next mind reading the B4 line would spend a session re-deriving this (Law 1). No ticket is cast for B4 and none should be. Next live item is B5.
